title: Charms: Amulet Sockets, Triggered Effects and Recharge
summary: Charms are socketable items for an amulet's Charm Socket. Each grants a bonus that triggers automatically when its condition is met (low life, critical hit, ailment, and more), then recharges. This guide covers charm properties, how to obtain and socket them, and which charm fits which build.
description: A source-linked reference for Charms in Path of Exile 2: amulet charm sockets, triggered effects, recharge, and how to choose a charm by build need.
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team
imageAlt: Path of Exile 2 Charm items - socketable amulet charms that trigger conditional effects

sections.title: Quick answer
sections.callout: Socket a Charm into your amulet's Charm Socket. When its trigger condition happens (e.g. you drop to Low Life, take a Critical Hit, or get an ailment), the charm's bonus fires automatically, then the charm recharges on a cooldown.
calloutDetail: Charms are automatic - you do not press anything; the effect fires when the condition is met.
After triggering, the charm goes on cooldown and recharges, so it is a periodic safety net rather than a always-on buff.

answers.label: Use for
text: A reactive defensive or utility layer on any amulet-wearing build.

answers.label: Check first
text: Confirm your amulet has a Charm Socket (some need unlocking via quest or bench).

answers.label: Avoid
text: Expecting a charm to act like a permanent aura - it triggers, then recharges.

facts.label: Socket
note: One charm per amulet in the current client.

facts.label: Trigger
note: Fires when its condition is met, no manual press.

facts.label: Recharge
note: Recharges after triggering; not always on.

facts.label: Types
note: Named by the effect they grant.

sections.title: Charm families
intro: Charms are grouped by the kind of bonus they grant. Each is named after its effect (for example a charm that grants Endurance Charges on Low Life). The exact catalogue grows with patches - use the in-game tooltip as the source of truth.

members.title: Defensive charms
body: Trigger on danger (Low Life, Critical Hit, ailment) to grant defences: Endurance Charges, a Barrier, or recovered Life.

members.title: Offensive charms
body: Trigger to grant Frenzy or Power Charges, or a burst of damage, when you meet the condition (kill, ailment applied, and so on).

members.title: Utility charms
body: Trigger to remove an ailment, restore Mana, or cleanse a debuff when the condition fires.

members.title: Elemental charms
body: Trigger on elemental events (being shocked, freezing an enemy) to turn the ailment into a benefit.

properties.label: Socket
notes: Charms slot into the dedicated Charm Socket on an amulet, not a regular gem socket.

properties.label: Trigger condition
notes: Each charm defines the event that sets it off: Low Life, Critical Hit taken, ailment, kill, and more.

properties.label: Effect
notes: When triggered, the charm grants its bonus (charges, Barrier, Life, cleanse) for a short duration.

properties.label: Recharge
notes: After firing, the charm goes on cooldown and recharges; it is a periodic safety net, not a permanent aura.

properties.label: One per amulet
notes: In the current client one amulet holds one charm. Confirm against your client if this changes.

sections.title: How to get Charms
intro: Charms enter the pool as endgame content tied to the amulet charm-socket system.

routes.label: Endgame drops
body: Charms drop from maps and bosses once the charm-socket content is available.

routes.label: Quest / unlock
body: Some amulets need a Charm Socket unlocked through a quest or bench step before a charm can be fitted.

routes.label: Trade
body: Buy specific charms from other players for the effect you want.

routes.label: Targeted farming
body: Community strategies (for example forcing 'Rite of Passage' style drops) can bias drops toward charm-related rewards.

steps.label: Unlock the socket
body: Make sure your amulet has a Charm Socket (quest or bench, depending on the item).

steps.label: Pick the charm
body: Choose a charm whose trigger and bonus match the danger your build actually faces.

steps.label: Socket it
body: Drag the charm into the amulet's Charm Socket like a gem.

steps.label: Confirm recharge
body: In combat, watch the charm fire on its condition and recharge afterwards.

sections.title: Where charms fit
note: Charms only go in an amulet's Charm Socket. They do not fit weapons, armour, or regular gem sockets.

items.fix: Unlock the socket via quest/bench first.

items.label: Trigger matches your risk
checks: Pick a trigger you actually encounter (Low Life, Crit, ailment).
items.why: A charm whose condition never fires does nothing.
items.fix: Match the charm to your real deaths or pressure points.

sections.title: Charms vs other options
paragraphs: Charms are often compared to Flasks. Flasks are active: you press them (or they auto-use) and they are consumed over their duration. Charms are passive and automatic: they fire on a condition and then recharge, so they cover the moment you forget to flask or cannot flask.

Charms are also distinct from Anointing (Distilled Emotions). Anointing grants a permanent Notable passive on the amulet; a charm grants a triggered, temporary bonus from the Charm Socket. They occupy different amulet systems and can coexist.
Against permanent auras or auras from skills, charms are weaker per-second but cost no mana and need no socket - they are a free reactive layer on top of your main setup.
bullets: Flask = active, consumed, you press it.
Anoint = permanent Notable; charm = triggered bonus (different socket).
Charm is a free reactive layer, not a main damage source.

sections.title: Which builds use which charm
intro: Pick the charm by the failure mode your build actually dies to, not by raw numbers.

builds.title: Glass-cannon attacker
builds.description: Defensive charm triggering on Low Life for a Barrier or Endurance Charges.

builds.title: Charge-stacking build
builds.description: Offensive charm that grants Frenzy or Power Charges when the condition hits.

builds.title: DoT / ailment build
builds.description: Utility charm that cleanses the ailment on trigger.

builds.title: Caster with mana issues
builds.description: Utility charm restoring Mana when you take a Critical Hit or drop low.

entries.question: I have a charm but my amulet has no Charm Socket - what do I do?
summary: A player had a charm but could not socket it.
editorialAnalysis: Charms require the amulet's Charm Socket. Some amulets need the socket unlocked via a quest or bench step before a charm can be fitted.
officialAnswer: Unlock the Charm Socket on the amulet first, then socket the charm.

entries.question: My charm never seems to trigger - is it broken?
summary: Players felt their charm did nothing.
editorialAnalysis: A charm only fires when its specific condition is met, then recharges. If the condition rarely happens in your content, the charm rarely fires - match the trigger to the danger you actually face.
officialAnswer: Choose a charm whose trigger matches the pressure your build meets.
